hierarchy.game: one dominant problem played until resolution, failure, equilibrium, deadlock or supersession
hierarchy.arc: a sequence of games linked by persistent consequences
hierarchy.world: persistent people, relationships, reputation, institutions, map and memory across all arcs

arc_question: What happens when a distributed statistical system produces a consequential result before the participating institutions agree on what counts as an error?

games.name: incident containment
games.main_question: Within 72 hours, what can be responsibly said and what should be paused or continued?
games.entry_trigger: suspicious low-risk row plus external screenshot
end_conditions: joint preliminary statement accepted for release
interim operational decision made: pause / narrow / continue-with-guardrails
or the institutions deadlock and an external authority imposes the interim decision

games.name: cause verification
games.main_question: Which parts of the incident can be reproduced, falsified or attributed to data, version, pipeline and statistical assumptions?
games.entry_trigger: containment decision creates a formal audit/validation mandate
end_conditions: technical causal graph reaches a stable evidence-supported form
or validation reaches a bounded statement of what cannot be distinguished with available evidence
games.successor_trigger: verified technical findings create responsibility, policy, contract or reputation consequences

games.name: responsibility allocation
games.main_question: Who had which duty at which stage, and what changes must be imposed on the system and institutions?
games.entry_trigger: audit findings are stable enough to support governance decisions
end_conditions: new decision rights / process rules / documentation duties assigned
or responsibility remains partially contested but the operating system changes anyway
games.successor_trigger: governance changes alter careers, relationships and institutional equilibrium

games.name: afterlife
games.main_question: Months later, what did the incident actually change in careers, trust, work design and the public story?
games.entry_trigger: operational crisis is over but consequences persist
end_conditions: the incident ceases to generate new material state changes
remaining disagreements become background commitments for future unrelated games
games.successor_trigger: none required; world continues with persistent writeback

anti_serialization_rules: Do not keep a game alive merely because unresolved facts exist.
A game ends when its dominant decision problem has converged; residual questions may seed the next game.
Do not introduce every core actor in Game 1.
New actors enter only when a successor game's jurisdiction reaches them.
A successor game must inherit at least one material consequence from its predecessor.
If an arc produces no persistent writeback, it was probably decorative filler.
